discovery.title: CPU Time Is Shared
discovery.summary: Round Robin gives each process a limited time quantum, then rotates unfinished processes back into the ready queue.

sections.title: What is Round Robin?
sections.content: Round Robin is a CPU scheduling method where ready processes take turns using the CPU.

sections.title: Time quantum
sections.content: A time quantum is the maximum amount of CPU time a process receives in one turn.

sections.title: Why processes take turns
sections.content: Taking turns stops one long process from keeping every other ready process waiting for too long.

sections.title: When a process is unfinished
sections.content: If a process still has work after its time quantum, it goes to the back of the ready queue.

sections.title: When a process finishes
sections.content: A process that uses all of its remaining time leaves the CPU and moves to Completed.

sections.title: Time-sharing systems
sections.content: Round Robin is useful when many users or programs should get regular chances to run.

sections.title: FCFS and Round Robin
sections.content: FCFS runs the first process until it finishes. Round Robin pauses unfinished processes after a time quantum so others can run.
